tickets.title: RF characterisation for the 1.4.2 supervisor-timing change
tickets.body: Request an outdoor/body-block/commuting RF soak re-characterisation for firmware 1.4.2's revised BLE supervisor timing, since lab validation only covered indoor office RF.
tickets.routing_rationale: The action requires designing and running an outdoor/body-block/commuting RF soak characterization for the revised BLE supervisor timing in firmware 1.4.2, which needs expertise in BLE radio link behavior under varying RF environments and body attenuation, plus firmware/RTOS-level knowledge of the connection-supervisor timing implementation to correctly instrument and interpret disconnect/reconnect events during the soak test. Priya Nair selected: overlap firmware-build, ble-radio, rtos; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Phone confound check on 1.4.2 disconnects
tickets.body: Re-run the firmware 1.4.1 vs 1.4.2 disconnect comparison with a clustered per-device confidence interval and a phone-OS/model stratification to rule out a phone-side confound analogous to the prior firmware train incident before attributing the rise to the firmware patch.
tickets.routing_rationale: This requires re-analyzing disconnect and session-gap telemetry with proper statistical treatment (clustered per-device confidence intervals), which is a data-quality/telemetry-pipeline analysis task, combined with knowledge of BLE connection-supervisor timing behavior and firmware build differences between 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 to correctly interpret whether phone-OS/model stratification reveals a device-side confound versus a genuine firmware-driven change in disconnect detection sensitivity. Tomasz Kowalski selected: overlap ble-radio, firmware-build; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Counted-events vs connected-time diagnostic
tickets.body: Add a paired counted-events-vs-connected-time diagnostic to the telemetry export so future supervisor-timing changes can be distinguished from real connectivity degradation without ad hoc analysis.
tickets.routing_rationale: Building a diagnostic that pairs counted disconnect events with connected-time/session-gap metrics requires telemetry pipeline design to instrument and export the new comparison, plus BLE radio/connection-supervisor expertise to correctly interpret what timing changes affect detection sensitivity, and firmware build familiarity to hook the diagnostic into the supervisor-timing logic across versions. Priya Nair selected: overlap firmware-build, ble-radio; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Continue monitoring skin-irritation volume
tickets.body: Continue routine monitoring of adhesion_flag rate and skin-irritation feedback tag volume week over week; re-open severity review if a firmware, region, or lot-specific concentration emerges.
tickets.routing_rationale: Ongoing monitoring requires someone who can interpret adhesion_flag and skin-irritation feedback trends against motion-intensity and thermal factors, understanding adhesive material behavior and wear/lift mechanics under mechanical stress. Data-quality expertise is needed to track week-over-week rate changes reliably and detect any emerging firmware, region, or lot-specific concentration that would warrant re-opening the severity review. Mei Chen selected: overlap adhesive-materials, wear-mechanics; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Lot split for skin-irritation tickets
tickets.body: Request lot/serial-level metadata for skin-irritation and adhesion tickets to test for concentration in a single production lot, per playbook guidance that a new cluster needs a lot split rather than a wave-away via the existing open characterization.
tickets.routing_rationale: The action requires pulling and analyzing lot/serial-level manufacturing metadata against adhesion/skin-irritation tickets to test for concentration in a single production lot. This needs adhesive-materials expertise to reason about lot-based defect mechanisms, wear-mechanics expertise to interpret how mechanical/adhesive failure could surface under high motion independent of thermal factors, and data-quality expertise to correctly join ticket records with lot/serial metadata and validate the resulting breakdown. Mei Chen selected: overlap adhesive-materials, wear-mechanics; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Do not close skin-irritation as expected
tickets.body: Remind support agents via the existing playbook not to close skin-irritation/adhesion tickets as expected behavior; continue offering replacement rings and logging tags as appropriate.
tickets.routing_rationale: The action updates a support playbook message about skin-irritation/adhesion tickets, so it requires copy-ops skill to word agent guidance accurately without overstating conclusions. The underlying subject matter concerns adhesive-lift and skin-contact wear behavior under motion, so adhesive-materials and wear-mechanics expertise is needed to ensure the reminder reflects an accurate, defensible characterization of the mechanism and its uncertainty, given the open question about motion-only versus thermal-driven irritation. Jonah Adeyemi selected: overlap wear-mechanics; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.routing_rationale: The action requires review and revision of on-screen wording that risks being misread as a clinical claim, which calls for expertise in regulatory-sensitive communications review and copy-editing/content operations for user-facing display text, consistent with prior comms-labeled incidents of this pattern. Hannah Briggs selected: overlap regulatory-comms, copy-ops; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Claims tickets by firmware and app version
tickets.body: Break down current-window claims-interpretation tickets by firmware_version and app_version to check for concentration around any specific UI copy change before concluding no release is implicated.
tickets.routing_rationale: This action requires breaking down ticket volumes by firmware and app version to check for concentration tied to a specific UI copy/wording change. That calls for expertise in interpreting claims-interpretation ticket content (claims-review), understanding how on-screen copy and wording changes are versioned and rolled out (copy-ops), and rigorous cross-tabulation and data-quality analysis to correctly segment tickets by version and window without conflating unrelated cohorts. Hannah Briggs selected: overlap claims-review, copy-ops; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Wellness-score clarification copy
tickets.body: If copy review confirms confusing wording, prepare an in-app or help-article clarification (not user-targeted medical messaging) reiterating the score is a wellness indication, consistent with the KD-03 staff script.
tickets.routing_rationale: Preparing a clarification for in-app or help-article content requires copy/UX writing expertise to revise wording so it cannot be misread as a clinical claim, plus claims-review expertise to ensure the revised language conforms to prior guidance (KD-03) on avoiding medical/diagnostic implications and aligns with regulatory-safe messaging standards. Luca Ferrara selected: overlap claims-review; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

tickets.title: Confirm overheating tag is a known cosmetic UI issue
tickets.body: Route 'overheating' tagged tickets through the existing battery/app-ui intake playbook (KI-UI-011 / KD-03) rather than a thermal-safety path, and consider re-tagging future tickets that clearly describe UI chrome or cold-weather drain as 'battery'/'app-ui' to reduce noise in the overheating tag.
tickets.routing_rationale: This is a triage-routing and tagging fix: work involves updating intake playbook routing logic and ticket-tag classification rules, which needs familiarity with the mobile app's battery-UI chrome/rendering behavior (to confirm the cosmetic warning pathway), and data-quality/taxonomy skill to redefine tagging criteria so future tickets describing UI chrome or cold-weather drain are correctly classified as battery/app-ui rather than overheating, reducing noise without suppressing genuine thermal signals. Samira El-Sayed selected: overlap data-quality; under capacity; roster order as remaining tie.

Since the current cluster traces to UI/battery-display mislabeling rather than hardware, familiarity with the mobile app's battery/UI rendering behavior is relevant to correctly interpreting any future step change.
